image.subject: a 1905 printed map of the British Empire in red, spread on a library table under a lamp, an old hand resting on its edge

storyboard.claim: The Edwardian elite wanted one English-speaking superstate tying Britain, America and the Dominions together.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A red-coloured imperial map on a library table.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens chunk 7 after the Illuminati and Edwardian club setup.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the three parts of the proposed federation.

storyboard.claim: Why should a viewer care about a handful of Edwardian men talking politics?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A plain question card.
storyboard.onScreenText: Why care about a private club?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the grand federation plan of 240.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the club as the hook for the whole argument.

image.subject: a lone man in a dark suit standing at a tall window of a stone London building in 1906, seen from behind, looking out at a grey city

storyboard.claim: A hierarchy that feels insecure starts to lose its grip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An Edwardian gentleman at a window, seen from behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the elite felt threatened, after the question in 241.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the British decline to a feeling of insecurity.

image.subject: a 1900s London street at dusk seen from behind, an everyman in a bowler hat looking toward a small lamplit club door among horse-drawn carriages

storyboard.claim: A declining power projects its fears onto a small, closed group.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A small lit club door on a dusky London street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the insecurity argument from 242.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the small group as the target of the fear.

image.subject: a candle-lit room where five Edwardian gentlemen in dark suits lean over a large map on a table, their faces half in shadow

storyboard.claim: Ambitious theorists get turned into a sinister global cabal in the public mind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Five men in shadow around a candle-lit map.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the transformation from 243.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualises the cabal the public imagined.

image.subject: a crowd of worried men in 1900s Paris, reading newspapers at a street kiosk on a grey evening

storyboard.claim: Politicians in France, Canada and America believed the Round Table was secretly running the world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A crowd of anxious readers at a Paris newsstand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the club to the public fear across countries.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the fear in Paris, one of the named countries.

image.subject: a wooden marionette's strings hanging down from a dark ceiling over a worn map of Europe, lit by one candle

storyboard.claim: The belief was that a hidden hand pulled all the strings of finance and war.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Puppet strings hanging over a map.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the cabal belief from 245.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visual metaphor for hidden control of finance and war.

image.subject: a late-18th-century Bavarian university professor in his late twenties, slim, powdered-hair style, dark frock coat with a white cravat, walking alone on a dusty country road away from a town

storyboard.claim: Over a decade after the Illuminati were destroyed, a panic about them erupted across Europe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Weishaupt alone on a dusty road leaving a Bavarian town.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the Illuminati origin from the start of the book.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the founder in exile, dead as an organisation.

image.subject: a stack of late-18th-century leather-bound books on a wooden desk, a quill and an inkwell beside them in a dim study

storyboard.claim: Two writers published sensational books about the Illuminati.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Old leather books and a quill on a study desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the panic spread, after 247.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the two authors Barruel and Robison (corrected from the ASR spelling).

storyboard.claim: The books claimed the Illuminati had not died and had gone further underground.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried statement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the claim the books made, after 248.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the sensational claim directly.

image.subject: a Parisian street at night with a crowd gathered around torch-lit doorways, a shuttered royal palace behind them, seen from a distance

storyboard.claim: The fall of the French monarchy was blamed on the Illuminati and Weishaupt's book.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A night crowd before a shuttered palace.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Escalates the claim from 249 to the French Revolution.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the blame in revolutionary Paris, without violence on screen.

image.subject: an empty candle-lit lodge room in the 1790s, rows of unoccupied wooden chairs around a table, a single candle burning, a map on the wall

storyboard.claim: The network was dead, with most members exiled or hiding, but the paranoia kept it alive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty lodge room with one candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the dead network with the belief in 250.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the empty room as the real state of the lodge.

storyboard.claim: The old monarchies needed a villain to explain the chaos of the Revolution.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried statement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the motive behind the panic in 251.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the political motive for the myth.

storyboard.claim: The honest explanation, that the peasants hated the rulers and the economy was mismanaged, was too hard to admit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quoted line on screen.
storyboard.onScreenText: The peasants hate us and we mismanaged the economy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the uncomfortable truth the rulers avoided, after 252.
storyboard.addedInformation: Quotes the implied admission as a single line.

image.subject: the enormous shadow of a seated man cast across a bare plastered wall of an empty room by a single candle

storyboard.claim: A small, dead club was inflated into a global menace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A giant shadow on an empty wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the admission in 253 with the inflation of the myth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualises the small club made huge in imagination.

storyboard.claim: Can the whole story be dismissed as pure paranoia? A historian says no.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host interrupts to challenge the dismissal, after 254.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the historian Carroll Quigley.

image.subject: a crowd of ordinary people seen from behind, facing a distant podium on a wintry public square under a flag

storyboard.claim: Quigley was influential enough that a US president quoted him in an inauguration speech.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A crowd facing a distant podium on a winter square.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why Quigley matters, after 255.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the quotation at a public inauguration.

image.subject: a dark government corridor of a 1930s British building, a single shaft of light falling on a closed office door

storyboard.claim: Quigley claimed the Round Table ran British foreign policy from the shadows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A closed door in a dark corridor with a shaft of light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States Quigley's claim, after 256.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visual for the hidden-control argument.

storyboard.claim: Quigley spent his career claiming secret power that shaped the twentieth century.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried statement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds Quigley's career claim, after 257.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the historian presented the group as a real threat.

image.subject: a long archive room of grey filing boxes and old government files on wooden shelves, a clerk's hand turning a yellowed page

storyboard.claim: Look at the historical record, where the grand plans failed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An archive with a hand on an old file.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from Quigley's claim to the evidence, after 258.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visual for checking the documents.

storyboard.claim: Did Britain form a unified federal English-speaking world?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card.
storyboard.onScreenText: Did Britain form a federal English-speaking world?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the grand plan to the test, after 259.
storyboard.addedInformation: Poses the question the answer to which is no.

image.subject: a single flagpole on a London government building roof against a dim evening sky, a flag being lowered at dusk

storyboard.claim: The British Empire fell apart, lost its dominions and its economic supremacy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flag lowered at dusk on a flagpole.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question in 260 with the outcome.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visual for the empire's decline.

storyboard.claim: Two world wars bankrupted Britain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A timeline from 1914 to 1945.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reasons for the decline in 261.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dates the two wars that drained the empire.

image.subject: an empty chair in a dark parliamentary chamber with green benches, lit by one lamp

storyboard.claim: The Round Table's power was an illusion, inflated by politicians looking for a scapegoat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty chair in a dim chamber.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the illusion argument from 262.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the politicians who needed someone to blame.

image.subject: a grand stone tower looming over an empty city square at dusk, a single small figure standing in the square below

storyboard.claim: The hierarchy, the tower, is having a nightmare about the square.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tall tower over a dusk square with one figure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Uses the book's tower-and-square metaphor, after 263.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the tower fearing the open square.

image.subject: a dark empty corridor of a grand stone building, a long shadow stretching across the floor toward a closed door

storyboard.claim: A hierarchy scared of what it cannot control invents a monster in the shadows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A long shadow across a dark corridor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the tower metaphor from 264.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visual for the fear-driven invention.

image.subject: an old ledger page with ink lines drawn between many names, a candle beside it on a wooden desk

storyboard.claim: Networks are not omnipotent cabals, but they do wield targeted power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A ledger page with ink lines linking names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Warns against dismissing networks entirely, after 265.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visualises a network as ink lines on a ledger.

image.subject: a lone figure seen from behind at a library desk, surrounded by stacked ledgers and open letters, a candle lit

storyboard.claim: Network power concentrates in one highly connected person who knows how to work the numbers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lone figure at a desk covered in ledgers and letters.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows from networks to one person, after 266.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the single hub at work.

image.subject: a 1970s government office with an old black rotary telephone and a row of ringing extension phones on a wooden desk

storyboard.claim: In the early 1970s the White House national security adviser became the individual hub of power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Rotary phones on an office desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the individual hub, after 267.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the scene in the White House in the early 1970s.

image.subject: an elderly American statesman in a dark suit, white hair combed back, heavy-framed glasses, seated at a wooden desk in a government office

storyboard.claim: The hub is Henry Kissinger, the national security adviser, at his desk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kissinger seated at his desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the individual from 268.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces Kissinger as the national security adviser.

image.subject: a crowded government desk covered with ringing telephones and paper files, a dark suit jacket hung over the back of the chair

storyboard.claim: He runs foreign policy from his own office, surrounded by ringing phones.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A desk crowded with phones and files.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the office operation, after 269.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the phone-driven machine without the official hierarchy.

image.subject: an empty corridor in a government building with a closed office door at the far end and no one in sight

storyboard.claim: He bypasses the official state hierarchy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty corridor leading to a closed door.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how he avoids the official chain, after 270.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visual for the route that skips the hierarchy.

image.subject: a private meeting in a dim Washington townhouse, two men in dark suits seen from behind across a small table with a single lamp

storyboard.claim: He back-channels directly with the Soviet ambassador Anatoly Dobrynin, not through the diplomatic tower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two men at a small table in a dim room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the concrete example of bypassing, after 271.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the Soviet ambassador correctly (ASR gave Anatoli de Brinion).

storyboard.claim: From one desk he works journalists, Hollywood producers and foreign dignitaries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-item list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Widens the back channel to every kind of contact, after 272.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the contacts he reaches on the private line.

image.subject: an elderly American statesman in a dark suit, white hair combed back, heavy-framed glasses, standing in a room where telephone cables run from his desk to every corner

storyboard.claim: Kissinger was not using a network, he was the network.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kissinger standing at the centre of phone cables.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the Kissinger example, after 273.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cables show him as the hub of every line.

storyboard.claim: The lesson applies to how power works today.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Text-carried statement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from history to the viewer's present, after 274.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the modern lesson.

image.subject: an ordinary person seen from behind at a small desk in a dim room, one candle lit, no other people around

storyboard.claim: Immense influence needs no standing army and no sprawling bureaucracy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: One person at a small candle-lit desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the modern lesson, after 275.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows a single person holding power with no organisation.

image.subject: an aerial view of city streets converging on one central square at dusk, all roads leading to the same point

storyboard.claim: A single highly connected hub can hold more influence than a bureaucratic tower.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Streets converging on one square from above.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines the hub, after 276.
storyboard.addedInformation: Visual for many lines meeting in one place.

left.label: TOWER
left.subject: a vast office block with thousands of identical lit windows at dusk, seen from the street

right.label: HUB
right.subject: a single person at a small candle-lit desk in a dark room, seen from behind

storyboard.claim: One well-connected individual can outweigh a bureaucratic tower of thousands.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Office block on the left, one lit desk on the right.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Compares the hub with the tower, after 277.
storyboard.addedInformation: Extends the point to the corporate world in the next line.

image.subject: the steps of a Georgia courthouse in the 1970s, a lawyer in a dark suit seen from behind walking up toward the door

storyboard.claim: Vernon Jordan began as a civil rights lawyer in Georgia, outside the corporate establishment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lawyer climbing courthouse steps.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the corporate example, after 278.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets Vernon Jordan's starting point outside the corporate world.
